args.goal: Using products/services/catalogue-qa/fulfillment/findings.json and procedure.md (synthetic execution TASK-179428356112/113), make the minimal EN/FR text correction to the agency QA section of products/sites/shopify-catalogue-example/index.html. The corrected text must say: (1) the preservation and image-mapping checks need the client's produced Shopify rows, and input-only requests get input validation only; (2) the report names failed checks, and the affected rows are located by hand; (3) the header and line-ending checks compare against our documented column subset, not Shopify acceptance. Change nothing else. Save a diff and a reverse-to-baseline check, run a PUBLISH_SITE dry_run, and stop at handing the exact digest to an independent reviewer. description:
I completed CATALOGUE-QA-FULFILLMENT-EXECUTION (BUILDER, TASK-179428356110 to 116). Everything here was tested on synthetic data only, and the public site files were not changed.

**What the tests showed**
- **Input rows only:** transform.py refused all 6 input defects I planted (duplicate SKU, duplicate barcode, duplicate color+size, bad price, non-http image URL, duplicate image row). The line-numbered errors appear only in the --report JSON; stdout gives just a count.
- **With the client's produced Shopify rows:** verify_example.py caught all 7 output defects (changed barcode, changed price, duplicate row, missing image, wrong variant image, unknown SKU, dropped row). The valid case passed all 12 checks.

**The advertised offer overstates three things**
- **Preservation and image checks need the produced rows.** Without them, the checks only test our own conversion, so they must not be reported to a client.
- **No row-level report.** The checker gives pass/fail per check with no row location, so failing rows have to be found by hand.
- **Format checks fail on harmless differences.** The header and line-ending checks fail on any extra column or Windows (CRLF) line endings. A failure only means the file differs from our column list; it does not mean Shopify would reject it.

Also, the tools do not enforce the 20-row cap: a 21-row input was accepted, so the cap has to be checked by hand at intake.

The procedure is in products/services/catalogue-qa/fulfillment/procedure.md and the findings in findings.json. I read both after saving them, and messaged DIRECTOR with the results.

**Why the next step changes:** the binding issue is that the public offer promises more than we can deliver, not a missing feature. So the next mission is a minimal correction of the offer text, which stops at an independent review of its exact digest before anything is deployed.

**Unchanged:** feedback is still unknown (5 unclassified sources), there is no request, order or revenue, and Treasury is unfunded. All observation and retirement deadlines still apply, including tender retirement and award-link removal at or after 2026-11-18T09:00Z and welfare retirement after 2026-12-04T17:00Z.
